items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

claims.text: CVE-2026-109618 involves a remote code execution vulnerability where handling out-of-memory errors via longjmp() leaves request memory uninitialized due to improper control flow management, allowing attackers to reliably achieve RCE using out-of-memory (OOM) triggers.

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.5.4, 19.4.6, 19.3.8
items.one_liner: Upgrade self-hosted GitLab installations immediately to patch a critical heap buffer overflow in bundled Git.
items.summary: GitLab released critical patch versions 19.5.4, 19.4.6, and 19.3.8 to address CVE-2026-105437, a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in bundled Git that can cause out-of-bounds heap writes and lead to arbitrary command execution within Gitaly. The vulnerability affects GitLab CE/EE versions from 16.2 prior to the new patches and was reported by user taise through the HackerOne bug bounty program. Self-compiled installations require manual updates to their Git binaries or upgrading the distribution Git package to version 2.56.1 or later. Cloud instances on GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched and require no user action.
key_facts: CVE-2026-105437: Heap-based buffer overflow in git
Minimum Git version for distribution package: 2.56.1
items.bottom_line: Self-managed GitLab instances must be updated immediately to prevent arbitrary command execution via a heap buffer overflow in Git.

items.title: iOS Sandbox Escape Is Public, and Apple Hasn’t Confirmed a Fix
items.one_liner: A public iOS sandbox escape flaw lets apps read other apps' files, prompting Binance wallet warnings and sideloaded exploit tools.
items.summary: A public iOS sandbox escape vulnerability, dubbed "worse_query," affects iOS versions 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2, allowing malicious apps to read local files from other apps and system containers. Published by researcher 'forcequitOS' via a proof-of-concept on GitHub, the flaw has been leveraged to build sideloaded file managers like WQ Files without requiring jailbreaks or kernel exploits. Binance issued a security warning noting that seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials across the ecosystem could be exposed, while Apple released security updates without explicitly mentioning a fix in its release notes.
items.bottom_line: An unconfirmed iOS sandbox escape vulnerability allows sideloaded apps to access other applications' local files and sensitive wallet data without a jailbreak.

items.title: Russian Turla Hackers Use New Cereal Malware to Steal Emails From Government Exchange Servers
items.one_liner: Russian Turla hackers use the modular Cereal toolset to silently harvest emails from Microsoft Exchange servers without external C2.
items.summary: The Russia-aligned state-sponsored threat actor Turla has been deploying a modular .NET cyber espionage toolset called Cereal to compromise Microsoft Exchange servers in Kazakhstan and Romania. Operating without external command-and-control infrastructure, the malware hides within legitimate Exchange processes, abuses serialization to transmit compiled .NET programs, and harvests emails via an automated collection module. The Cereal framework consists of eight interconnected components—including CerealRunner, CerealLoader, CerealSprinter, and CerealNeuron—designed for long-term, stealthy intelligence gathering.
key_facts: Target entities: Government entities in Kazakhstan and Romania
items.bottom_line: Turla threat actors are exploiting Microsoft Exchange servers using the stealthy Cereal .NET framework for long-term email espionage.

items.title: Vanderbilt University reels following ransomware attack claimed by BYOD group
items.one_liner: Ransomware group BYOD claims responsibility for a cyberattack on Vanderbilt University compromising over a million SSNs.
items.summary: Vanderbilt University suffered a ransomware attack claimed by a recently emerged extortion group known as BYOD, compromising extensive personal data including over one million Social Security numbers. The incident forced the university to take various digital services offline and instruct users to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. While core services like Wi-Fi, Okta, Outlook, and Zoom have been restored for safe use, students and faculty remain concerned about data extortion and the university's communication gaps.

items.title: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
items.one_liner: AI-native penetration framework ARTEX was observed actively exploiting compromised AWS credentials and public Cognito pools to hunt for financial data.
items.summary: Datadog Security Labs reported in-the-wild activity by ARTEX—an AI-native autonomous penetration framework developed by a Chinese creator—targeting AWS environments to harvest financial data and credentials in October 2026. Operating through hosted web consoles and LLM agent teams, ARTEX utilizes compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs via FilterLogEvents and abuses public Amazon Cognito user pools for anonymous sign-ups and account enumeration. Originally published on GitHub in July 2026 and closed-source after surpassing 12,000 forks, the platform accepts API keys for multiple LLM providers such as OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Anthropic, dynamically switching providers if keys are revoked.
key_facts: Target platforms: AWS (CloudWatch, Cognito), Okta, Entra ID
Supported LLM providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Qwen
items.bottom_line: The AI-native exploitation framework ARTEX is actively weaponizing LLM agent teams against cloud environments and identity providers.

items.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
items.one_liner: A senior US Army soldier stationed at a strategic NATO headquarters in the UK has been arrested for suspected espionage on behalf of Russia.
items.summary: British counter-terrorism police have arrested a 41-year-old senior US Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia. The detainee was posted at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, which houses the headquarters of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. He was taken into custody under sections one and three of the National Security Act 2023 for obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service. FBI Director Kash Patel emphasized the gravity of the espionage allegations, noting zero tolerance for personnel violating their oath and compromising allied security.

items.title: Jenkins Security Advisory 2026-10-28
items.one_liner: Jenkins security advisories highlight critical deserialization, XSS, and arbitrary file read vulnerabilities leading to potential remote code execution.
items.summary: Jenkins has released a security advisory detailing multiple vulnerabilities across its core and plugin deliverables related to XML serialization, XStream filtering, and configuration handling. Specifically, older versions fail to apply custom deserialization filters to resolves-to attributes, allow stored cross-site scripting via unconstrained collection element types in job config files, and mishandle command agent launchers and symbolic links during item renames. These flaws can allow authenticated attackers with specific configuration permissions to achieve remote code execution on the controller file system.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Jenkins to version 2.588 or LTS 2.580.2 immediately to fix critical XStream deserialization and file-handling flaws.

items.title: Critical vulnerabilities in N-able N-central prompt hosted shutdown
items.one_liner: Critical vulnerabilities in N-able N-central have prompted emergency downtime and urgent mitigation warnings for MSPs.
items.summary: N-able has responded to the public disclosure of 33 critical vulnerabilities—dubbed Able2Shell—affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform by taking hosted environments offline. Organizations operating on-premises servers have been urged to take them offline immediately pending a security hotfix.

CVE-2026-116779 is a code injection vulnerability in SignalWire FreeSWITCH enabling remote command execution via crafted SIP messages. CVE-2026-123158 is an authentication bypass vulnerability in OpenSSH affecting Linux systems using the musl C library. CVE-2026-123218 involves incorrect authorization checks in IBM Aspera Faspex 5 allowing authenticated users to escalate privileges.

items.title: ZDI-26-904: NVIDIA Megatron-LM Checkpoint Deserialization of Untrusted Data Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: If you are using Megatron-LM for LLM training, update to 0.17.1 immediately to prevent RCE via malicious model checkpoints.
items.summary: NVIDIA has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its Megatron-LM framework, identified as ZDI-26-904. The flaw exists in the checkpoint parsing logic, which fails to properly validate user-supplied data, allowing for deserialization of untrusted data. items.title: CPython: [CVE-2026-115559] imaplib STARTTLS serves plaintext bytes buffered before the handshake as if they came over TLS
items.one_liner: A buffer handling flaw in Python's imaplib allows attackers to inject forged responses into STARTTLS-protected IMAP sessions.
items.summary: A medium-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-115559) has been identified in Python's imaplib library, affecting versions 3.14.0 and later. The flaw occurs because the library fails to clear its read-ahead buffer after a STARTTLS handshake, allowing plaintext bytes received before the handshake to be processed as if they were protected by TLS. An attacker can exploit this to inject forged IMAP responses, such as CAPABILITY or tagged completion commands, into the client's session. Users are advised to update their Python environments to mitigate this injection risk.
items.bottom_line: Applications using imaplib for STARTTLS connections are vulnerable to command injection if they rely on the library's internal buffering.

items.one_liner: A buffer length calculation error in Zephyr's HTTP/2 server allows remote attackers to trigger memory corruption or RCE.
items.summary: The Zephyr HTTP/2 server contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in its static-filesystem handler. The flaw is triggered when the server incorrectly uses the file size as a buffer length, allowing an attacker to overflow the fixed-size receive buffer. This can lead to memory corruption, device crashes, or remote code execution by overwriting critical control data in the server's address space.

items.title: CVE-2026-77685 - Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM: integer underflow in the MCC TEST command handler leads to out-of-bounds read disclosed to the peer and out-of-bounds write
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-77685 is a Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM integer underflow allowing memory disclosure and host crashes via malformed frames.
items.summary: A high-severity integer underflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-77685) has been identified in the Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM multiplexer control-channel handler. Malformed UIH frames can cause the echo length calculation to underflow and narrow to 255, resulting in an out-of-bounds read that discloses adjacent stack or pool memory to a peer, as well as an out-of-bounds write that can crash the Bluetooth host. The flaw is reachable by an unpaired BR/EDR device within radio range. Two separate fixes are required to fully eliminate the underflow and prevent residual transmit buffer overruns.
key_facts: Vulnerability type: Integer underflow, out-of-bounds read/write
items.bottom_line: Unpaired nearby attackers can trigger memory disclosure and crash Bluetooth hosts via unauthenticated RFCOMM frames unless both patch fixes are applied.

claims.text: The RFCOMM multiplexer control-channel handler in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/rfcomm.c computed the echo length for a BT_RFCOMM_TEST command as buf->len - 1 and passed it to rfcomm_send_test()...
claims.support_span: The RFCOMM multiplexer control-channel handler in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/rfcomm.c computed the echo length for a BT_RFCOMM_TEST command as buf->len - 1 and passed it to rfcomm_send_test(), whose length parameter is a uint8_t.

claims.text: The resulting 255-byte TEST response is transmitted back to the attacker, disclosing roughly 255 bytes of adjacent stack/pool memory... and the accompanying out-of-bounds write corrupts memory following the transmit buffer...
claims.support_span: The resulting 255-byte TEST response is transmitted back to the attacker, disclosing roughly 255 bytes of adjacent stack/pool memory — including the contents of neighbouring receive buffers, which an attacker can prime with earlier packets — and the accompanying out-of-bounds write corrupts memory following the transmit buffer, which can crash the Bluetooth host.

items.title: CVE-2026-126186 - Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file read and remote code execution in Active Storage video previews, analysis and image processing

The flaw occurs because Active Storage uses file extensions to select decoders for video and image processing tools like FFmpeg and ImageMagick. An attacker can upload a malicious file with a deceptive extension to trigger unintended code execution or file disclosure. This affects applications that process user-uploaded media using these tools.
items.bottom_line: If your application uses Active Storage to process user-uploaded media, you must update to version 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2 immediately to prevent RCE.

items.one_liner: NTLM relay bypass against enforced LDAP signing exposes Windows Server 2016-2025 to complete domain compromise.
items.summary: SpecterOps researchers discovered a vulnerability (CVE-2026-70229) allowing NTLM relay attacks against LDAP connections even when LDAP signing is enforced. By establishing a signed connection, capturing a valid session key, and relaying a victim's NTLM authentication into an existing SASL record, attackers can execute malicious LDAP commands with the victim's privileges. This bypass affects all Windows Server versions from 2016 to 2025 and permits complete domain compromise via computer takeover primitives. Microsoft released a patch for the LDAP variant in October 2026 following an independent patch for SMB in September 2026.
items.bottom_line: NTLM authentication can be successfully relayed over existing signed LDAP connections, bypassing signing protections and enabling full domain compromise.

items.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale
items.one_liner: Agent Substrate is a CNCF Sandbox runtime designed to scale Kubernetes for idle-heavy AI agents.
items.summary: Agent Substrate is an open-source, zero-trust runtime donated to the CNCF Sandbox to address Kubernetes' inefficiencies when running autonomous AI agents and coding assistants at scale. Because traditional Kubernetes Pod lifecycles introduce multi-second cold starts and hold idle memory, Agent Substrate multiplexes many agent sessions across a smaller pool of persistent worker Pods. Idle sessions are snapshotted—including memory and filesystems via gVisor or microVMs—and restored onto available workers without hitting the API server or scheduler. This architecture achieves tenfold higher density and eliminates the latency overhead of turning agent steps into ephemeral containers.
key_facts: Density improvement: 10x higher density than standard containers

items.title: Xen Security Advisory 531 v1 (CVE-2026-99286) - Linux xen-netback: guest can trigger use-after-free for network statistics reads
items.one_liner: Xen and Linux environments running vhost-net or xen-netback need immediate patching to prevent guest-to-host DoS via use-after-free.
items.summary: A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-99286 (XSA-531) in the Linux xen-netback driver allows a guest to trigger a use-after-free when reading network statistics. The issue occurs due to missing RCU synchronization when tearing down queues after an error caused by illegal Xenstore data filled in by a guest. If statistics are read via sysfs during this teardown phase, it can lead to a driver or entire host crash, resulting in a Denial of Service. Linux versions 4.11 and newer are vulnerable, and mitigation requires using a userspace PV network backend or a dedicated network driver domain per guest.
items.bottom_line: Guests can crash Xen virtualization hosts via use-after-free in the xen-netback network statistics driver code.

claims.text: Linux versions 4.11 and newer are vulnerable.

items.one_liner: A Perl Web::Simple vulnerability allows XSS via improper escaping of single quotes in HTML attributes.
items.summary: A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability (CVE-2026-120212) has been discovered in the Perl module Web::Simple, affecting versions prior to 0.037. The issue stems from the library's failure to properly escape single quotes when generating HTML attributes. An attacker who can control input interpolated into a single-quoted attribute can break out of the attribute context and inject malicious scripts. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.037 or use double-quoted attributes as a temporary workaround.

items.bottom_line: Applications using Web::Simple to generate HTML must upgrade to version 0.037 to prevent XSS attacks via single-quoted attributes.

items.title: Onus on Uttar Pradesh to ensure undertrials allowed bail are released, says Supreme Court
items.one_liner: The Supreme Court ruled that Uttar Pradesh must secure the release of bailed undertrials languishing due to poverty.
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that the state government of Uttar Pradesh bears the legal onus to ensure that undertrial prisoners granted bail are not kept in custody simply due to their inability to meet financial release conditions. A Bench led by Justice M.M. Sundresh noted that out of 264 undertrial prisoners granted bail across 20 of the state's 75 districts, 106 remained incarcerated due to lack of financial security or guarantors. Analysis of 110 droppers revealed a self-describing vault-config.json file containing plaintext keys that decrypt a ZIP containing the payload. The payload shares a single signing certificate across 57 distinct variants while baking unique operator accounts, handles, and enrollment codes into the DEX constants. The malware reports these owner details back to its C2 on every foreground-app event, allowing analysts to map entire operator rosters from a single sample.
items.bottom_line: YuanKong Android RAT builds contain hardcoded operator credentials and cleartext configuration files, enabling attribution and roster extraction from single binaries.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-0311 in Checkov by Prisma Cloud allows local unauthenticated users to trigger server-side request forgery attacks against internal services.
items.summary: A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability designated CVE-2026-0311 has been found in Palo Alto Networks Checkov by Prisma Cloud versions 3.2.0 up to 3.2.533. The flaw allows a local, unauthenticated user to make unauthorized network requests from the host to internal services. Palo Alto Networks rated the severity as LOW with a CVSS base score of 4.8 and a CVSS-BT score of 1.1, noting no active exploitation. The product automatically updates, but users are advised to avoid running Checkov over untrusted content or to pass configurations explicitly via trusted configuration files as a mitigation.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.summary: AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex generate comprehensive and accurate pull request descriptions that can overwhelm readers with excessive technical detail. items.summary: Following disclosure discussions on the oss-security list regarding sblim-sfcb, the reporter clarified that the CIM-XML parser flaw does not cause a remote denial of service for the whole broker. items.bottom_line: The sblim-sfcb CIM-XML parser bug only affects isolated child processes, making it a robustness issue rather than a full remote DoS vulnerability.

items.summary: A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index. An extremely long path in a repository can pass Git's safety check, but Git then writes it to disk under a shorter name that an attacker can set to .git. This lets an attacker replace a submodule's .git file with a symbolic link to a folder holding malicious hooks or configuration.

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.one_liner: A developer used Claude Code to build an acoustic triangulation web app inspired by academic research to locate a mysterious beeping device.
items.summary: Faced with a mysterious, intermittently beeping device buried in a box room, software developer Simon Willison used Claude Code to build 'Beep Locator,' a software system that triangulates the source of acoustic signals using multiple commodity devices. Running on a Python web server with client interfaces connected via WebSockets, the app utilizes device-to-device audio ranging inspired by the 2007 research paper 'BeepBeep' by Chunyi Peng et al. items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have enabled state-of-the-art LLMs to be scaled to hundreds of billions of parameters, but they come with a fundamental and costly caveat: every expert MLP must occupy memory at inference time, even though the vast majority are idle for any given token. For example, Qwen3.5-122B has 256 experts in each of its 48 MoE layers, and 95% of its ~250 GB parameter memory footprint is taken up entirely by these expert MLPs alone. However, for any given token, only 8 experts in each layer are actually used. Expert pruning is one of the most direct fixes to this memory bottleneck. That is, permanently delete the least useful experts.

items.summary: Summary Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported. items.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
items.one_liner: Tamil Nadu's decision to disband the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations has drawn criticism as an unconvincing, politically motivated move.
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government abruptly disbanded the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and transferred its mandate to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission. The decision has drawn criticism for lacking a compelling rationale, especially given that the committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigor and submitted Part I of its report in February. State justifications citing the committee's non-statutory status or an overlap in functions with the Law Commission are unconvincing because the Law Commission is also established by executive order and lacks precedent in examining Centre-State relations. Opposition leaders and observers note that the move appears to be a politically motivated reversal rather than a reasoned administrative choice.

items.title: World Wars and India’s sacrifice
items.one_liner: India's immense military contributions to both World Wars remain largely uncommemorated domestically despite historic deployments and casualties.
items.summary: While many Commonwealth countries observe Remembrance Day to honor the fallen of the World Wars, India maintains an uneasy relationship with the occasion, largely treating it as an ordinary day despite its massive historical contribution. Undivided British India deployed 1.5 million troops in World War I, sustaining 74,000 casualties, and raised a volunteer army of 2.5 million personnel during World War II with up to 89,000 fatalities. Unlike World War I where troops fought predominantly in distant regions, approximately 700,000 Indian soldiers defended domestic territory during World War II when Japanese forces invaded the country in March 1944. This substantial sacrifice highlights India's critical historical role in combating fascism.
items.bottom_line: Acknowledging historical wartime contributions reinforces a nation's understanding of its profound impacts on global geopolitical shifts.

items.title: Keralam at 70: holding a mirror to India

items.summary: Keralam has transformed from one of India's poorest states in 1956 into one of its richest, achieving an infant mortality rate lower than the United States and a Human Development Index ranking that places it well ahead of China and 55 ranks above the Indian national average. In contrast, the national development framework remains focused on income-based measures, with national infant mortality levels remaining significantly higher than Keralam's. If the rest of India matched Keralam's infant mortality levels, over 500,000 infant lives would be saved annually.
